title: Inverse Galois theory and arithmetic fundamental groups, Part II: Hurwitz homological stability
summary: This continuation develops homological stability for nonsplitting Hurwitz spaces and the resulting uniform etale Betti bound. It starts with the braid-orbit monoid, left Hurwitz action, configuration spaces and four marked/full-monodromy Hurwitz variants of InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups. readme:
This continuation develops homological stability for nonsplitting Hurwitz spaces and the resulting uniform etale Betti bound. It starts with the braid-orbit monoid, left Hurwitz action, configuration spaces and four marked/full-monodromy Hurwitz variants of InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups. The new work is the component algebra and central sum, the graded K-complex with uniform estimates, the truncated based-arc resolution, the spectral sequence, and the homological induction. The endpoint includes full monodromy and center-free unmarked quotients, then a dimension estimate in tame finite characteristic.

General singular/cellular homology, bundles, transfer and connectivity belong to AlgebraicTopology; smooth embeddings and diffeomorphism groups belong to GeometricTopology; generic mapping classes are imported through MappingClassGroupsAndCanonicalRepresentations from LV.5; internally graded noncommutative module and derived-tensor machinery belongs to DGAInfinity. Each required adapter is an explicit request where the supplier text alone does not yet provide it. The arithmetic Hurwitz schemes and fixed-degree mod-L/coefficient-tower comparisons remain in parent IG.5. This roadmap uses the central sum of EVW, with corrected indices, module sides and constants. Its output does not include a Frobenius-equivariant algebraic stabilization or a fixed-q Cohen–Lenstra limit.

The six layers develop components, graded support and Tor bounds, disc arcs, the arc spectral sequence, linear stability, and uniform Betti estimates. Detailed target statements, APIs, checks and worked examples are in [the roadmap document](../readmes/InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroupsPartII.md). The independent Merkurjev–Scavia nonlifting direction is preserved as a split proposal in the blueprint; none of its49 items is treated as a result of this continuation.

stages.title: Nonsplitting classes and the central component operator
stages.description:
Nonsplitting conjugacy classes: For a subset c of a group G, Nonsplitting(c) means: c is one nonempty whole G-conjugacy class, its generated subgroup is G, and for every subgroup H<=G the intersection c∩H is empty or one H-conjugacy class. Equivalently, after the first two conditions, any g,h in c∩H are conjugate by an element of H. The intersection is automatically H-conjugation invariant.

The involution example: If |G|=2s with s odd, the elements of order2 form one conjugacy class c. If c generates G, then c is nonsplitting. In particular the transposition class of S3 satisfies the stability hypotheses.

Gluing of marked Hurwitz covers: Use the parent Borel models Hur_n=EB_n×_(B_n)c^n. Block inclusion B_n×B_m->B_(n+m) and concatenation c^n×c^m->c^(n+m) induce gluing Hur_n×Hur_m->Hur_(n+m), associative and unital up to compatible homotopies, equivariant for simultaneous G-conjugation. The external homology cross product followed by gluing yields the graded homology multiplication. It preserves the c-valued condition and sends monodromy subgroups H,K to <H,K>.

The graded component ring: Import S=disjoint_union_n c^n/B_n with concatenation from IG.3, and define R as native MonoidAlgebra k S. Give it the length grading R_n=k[S_n], augmentation R->k projecting to R_0=k, G-action by conjugation, and boundary G-grading. Set r_g=single([g],1). Its presentation is the free associative k-algebra on r_g (g∈c) modulo r_g r_h=r_(g h g^-1) r_g. Gluing identifies R with direct_sum_n H_0(Hur_n;k), as a graded algebra.

The central stabilization sum: For D>=1 set z_g=r_g^d and U_D=sum_(g∈c) z_g^D. The element U_D has degree a=Dd, is central, is fixed by simultaneous G-conjugation, and has boundary degree1. No normalization scalar is used. On any graded left R-module its action is a homogeneous k-linear map of degree a.

Stability on components: If c is nonsplitting, there are D>=1 and N>=0 depending only on (G,c), such that U_D:R_n->R_(n+a) is an isomorphism for every n>=N and every coefficient field in which |G| is invertible. Thus R[U_D] and R/U_DR have finite support. D may be chosen simultaneously for all nonempty generating intersections c∩H in subgroups H, and any positive multiple of the resulting permutation exponent is admissible after increasing N.

stages.title: Graded K-complexes and homological degree bounds
stages.description:
Support degree and internal shift: Specialize the imported graded-module interface to nonnegatively internally graded left and right R-modules, with morphisms of internal degree0. For a family V define SupportedLE(V,b) by V_n=0 for n>b. Use support degree in extended integers with deg0=-infinity. The internal shift M[q] has M[q]_n=M_(n-q), zero if n<q; a homogeneous map of degree a is a degree-zero map M[a]->N. Homological complexes retain a distinct nonnegative chain index. The native GradedObject supplies the family carrier; module structures and shift functors are imported from DGAInfinity.

Central torsion and stability defects: For a graded left R-module M let M[U]=ker(U:M->M), regarded in the source grading, and M/UM the cokernel in the target grading. Put Rbar=R/UR, with its native induced R-bimodule and augmentation, H_i^aug(M)=Tor_i^R(k,M), A(M)=max(deg M[U],deg M/UM), and delta(M)=max(deg Tor_0^R(Rbar,M),deg Tor_1^R(Rbar,M)). Choose A1>=max(1,a,A(R)), A2=A1+a, A0=5A1+A2. Finite support of these defects is the meaning of eventual U-stability, with separate source and target cutoffs.

Change of rings for the central quotient: For every nonnegative graded left R-module M there is an internal-degree-preserving first-quadrant spectral sequence E2_(i,j)=Tor_i^Rbar(k,Tor_j^R(Rbar,M)) converging in each total degree to Tor_(i+j)^R(k,M). The inner Tor is a left Rbar-module. Obtain it by specializing the supplier derived-tensor composition comparison to R->Rbar->k; no commutativity of R is assumed.

A balanced tensor support estimate: For a nonnegative graded right R-module N and left R-module M, deg(N tensor_R M)<=deg N+deg H_0^aug(M), whenever the right side is finite; the zero cases vanish. The same statement holds for the central quotient Rbar.

Tor support over the finite central quotient: For a nonnegative graded left Rbar-module V, deg Tor_i^Rbar(k,V)<=i deg Rbar+deg V for every i>=0 when these degrees are finite. It is enough, and is the uniform bound used below, to replace deg Rbar by A1.

Bounding central torsion by quotient Tor: For every nonnegative graded left R-module M, A(M)<=delta(M)+A1. More precisely there is an exact-at-the-middle sequence R[U] tensor_R M -> M[U] -> Tor_1^R(Rbar,M), whose first map has internal degree0 and second map has internal degree a.

Higher central-quotient Tor estimates: For i>=0 and nonnegative graded left R-module M, deg Tor_i^R(Rbar,M)<=delta(M)+A1 i.

Graded Nakayama with support control: For every nonnegative graded left Rbar-module V with finite degree of k tensor_Rbar V, deg V<=deg(k tensor_Rbar V)+deg Rbar. In particular k tensor_Rbar V=0 implies V=0.

Low augmentation Tor controls the defect: For every nonnegative graded left R-module M, delta(M)<=max(deg H_0^aug(M),deg H_1^aug(M))+4A1.

A general right-module Tor bound: If N is a nonnegative graded right R-module and M a nonnegative graded left R-module, then deg Tor_i^R(N,M)<=deg N+max(deg H_0^aug(M),deg H_1^aug(M))+A1 i+4A1, for all i>=0 with finite displayed degree bounds.

The Hurwitz K-complex: For a nonnegative graded left R-module M define a homological complex K(M) with K(M)_q=k[c^q] tensor_k M[q] for every q>=0. On a basis tensor with (q+1)-tuple (g_0,...,g_q), d sends it to sum_i (-1)^i (g_0,...,omit g_i,...,g_q) tensor r_(g_i^(g_(i+1)...g_q)) m. The empty suffix is1. Differential preserves internal grading and lowers chain degree by1. Degree-zero R-linear maps of M induce chain maps. For M=R this is a complex of free graded right R-modules.

Right linearity and tensor comparison: For every chain degree q, the right action on K(R)_q commutes with d. Evaluation of the balanced tensor induces a natural degreewise isomorphism of complexes K(R) tensor_R M ≅ K(M). It is compatible with internal shift and the k-linear U-action.

Null-homotopies for positive generators: For g∈c define a k-linear homotopy S_g on the tuple-orbit basis of K(R). For a tuple w of length q and monoid basis element s with boundary b, put S_g(w;s)=(g^((boundary(w)b)^-1),w;s). It raises chain degree and internal degree by1, extends linearly in s, and satisfies d S_g+S_g d = right multiplication by r_g. No right R-linearity of S_g is required or claimed.

The positive ideal kills regular K-homology: For every q>=0, the graded right R-module H_q(K(R)) is annihilated by R_positive. In particular right multiplication by U, and hence its equal left action on coefficients, is zero on homology.

Regular K-homology has linear support: For every q>=0, deg H_q(K(R))<=A2+q. In particular the first two K-homology groups of R have finite degree.

Universal coefficients for the K-complex: For M as above, the right-free complex K(R) gives a first-quadrant spectral sequence E2_(i,j)=Tor_i^R(H_j(K(R)),M) converging to H_(i+j)(K(M)), preserving internal grading. Consequently deg H_q(K(M))<=max(deg H_0^aug(M),deg H_1^aug(M))+A1 q+4A1+A2. This bound uses the chosen A1>=1.

Low K-homology controls augmentation Tor: There is a natural isomorphism H_0^aug(M) ≅ H_0(K(M)), and a natural surjection H_1(K(M)) -> H_1^aug(M), preserving internal grading. Thus deg H_i^aug(M)<=deg H_i(K(M)) for i=0,1.

Higher K-homology from two low degrees: Write h_i=deg H_i(K(M)). If h_0 and h_1 are finite, then for every q>1, h_q<=max(h_0,h_1)+A0 q. In the zero-low-homology case use the support formulation, which also forces the higher groups to vanish.

Stabilization from low K-homology: If b>=max(deg H_0(K(M)),deg H_1(K(M))) is a finite nonnegative integer, U:M_n->M_(n+a) is an isomorphism for every n>=b+A0. For M=R such a b exists. All constants depend only on (G,c) and the fixed admissible D, not on the permitted coefficient field.

stages.title: The truncated arc resolution
stages.description:
The marked-disc braid adapter: For the oriented compact smooth disc with n interior marked points, take orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms fixing the boundary pointwise and preserving the marked set setwise. Import their C-infinity topological group from GeometricTopology and their isotopy-class mapping group from the mapping-class supplier. Construct the compatible isomorphisms pi_0 Diff^+(D,P;boundary) ≅ Mod(D,P;boundary) ≅ TauCeti.BraidGroup n ≅ pi_1(Conf_n). A native sigma_i corresponds to the positive half twist interchanging the two adjacent marked points; pure mapping classes and full twists are different.

The based arc complex: Fix a boundary basepoint star on D and n distinct interior points P. A vertex is the isotopy class relative to star and P of a smooth embedded arc from star to one marked point, with interior in int(D) minus P and inward non-tangent initial derivative. A q-simplex is a collection of q+1 such classes with representatives disjoint away from star and with distinct marked endpoints and distinct ordered inward tangent rays near star. Order the vertices by their counterclockwise rays at star. Deleting an arc gives its semisimplicial faces. There are no q-simplices for q>=n. Orientation-preserving boundary-fixed marked diffeomorphisms act, and the action descends to B_n through the disc adapter.

The truncated braid-coset model: For n,q>=0 let L_(n,q) be the subgroup of B_n generated by the classical generators sigma_(q+2),...,sigma_(n-1). Empty generator ranges give the trivial subgroup; for q<n its shifted-strand inclusion identifies it with B_(n-q-1). Define A(n)_q=B_n/L_(n,q) if q<n and the empty set if q>=n. The quotient is by left cosets, with B_n acting by left multiplication. For q>=1 and q<n define s_(q,i)=sigma_(i+1)...sigma_q and face_i(bL_q)=b s_(q,i)L_(q-1), 0<=i<=q; s_(q,q)=1. Add the unique augmentation A(n)_0->point.

Coset faces satisfy semisimplicial identities: The faces in the truncated coset model are independent of the representative and B_n-equivariant. For q>=2 and 0<=i<j<=q, face_i face_j=face_(j-1) face_i. Together with augmentation these make A(n) an augmented semisimplicial B_n-set, of dimension n-1 if n>0. No degeneracy maps are asserted.

Arc stabilizers and the coset identification: For 0<=q<n, B_n acts transitively on ordered q-simplices of the geometric arc complex. The stabilizer of the standard fan of q+1 straight arcs is exactly L_(n,q). The maps bL_q -> b applied to the standard fan are equivariant bijections compatible with all faces and augmentation, hence identify the geometric and truncated coset semisimplicial sets.

Connectivity of the arc resolution: For n>=1, the geometric arc realization, and hence |A(n)|, is (n-2)-connected. For n=1 the convention means nonempty; for n=2 it means path connected. For n=0 retain the explicitly empty complex. Only this connectivity, not a stronger contractibility assertion, is used.

stages.title: The arc spectral sequence for Hurwitz homology
stages.description:
Graded Hurwitz homology modules: For p>=0 define M_p=direct_sum_(n>=0) H_p(Hur_n;k), internally graded by n. Give it the left R-action induced by the degree-zero part of homology multiplication under gluing. Then M_0=R as a graded left module, and simultaneous G-conjugation is an action on M_p compatible with the R-action and U. In each fixed n its homology is finite dimensional by the finite-cell bound in HS.5; that finiteness is not used to define M_p.

The Borel arc resolution: For each n form the semisimplicial space X(n)_q=EB_n×_(B_n)(A(n)_q×c^n) and its thick realization X(n). Its augmentation to Hur_n has, in the covering-bundle model, fibre |A(n)|. For n>=2 the augmentation induces an isomorphism H_t(X(n);k)->H_t(Hur_n;k) whenever t<n-2. Its skeletal filtration is bounded by n-1 in the semisimplicial direction.

Identification of arc rows with K-terms: For 0<=q<n, X(n)_q is homotopy equivalent to c^n//L_q and then to c^(q+1)×Hur_(n-q-1). This gives H_p(X(n)_q;k) ≅ (K(M_p)_(q+1))_n. Under these identifications the face induced by bL_q->b s_(q,i)L_(q-1) acts on tuples by s_(q,i)^-1; it removes g_i from the first q+1 entries and prefixes g_i^(g_(i+1)...g_q) to the residual tuple. Thus the alternating face differential is exactly K differential.

The Hurwitz arc spectral sequence: The skeletal filtration of X(n) gives a first-quadrant homological spectral sequence E1_(q,p)=H_p(X(n)_q;k)=(K(M_p)_(q+1))_n for p,q>=0, vanishing for q>=n, with d1 the alternating face map and d_r of bidegree(-r,r-1). It converges to H_(p+q)(X(n);k). For p+q<n-2 its abutment identifies with H_(p+q)(Hur_n;k). For q>0, E2_(q,p)=(H_(q+1)K(M_p))_n; E2_(0,p)=coker(K(M_p)_2->K(M_p)_1)_n.

The low K-homology edge sequence: For every p,n there is an exact sequence 0->(H_1 K(M_p))_n -> E2_(0,p) -> (M_p)_n -> (H_0 K(M_p))_n ->0, where the middle map is induced by the K differential K1->K0 and equals the augmentation edge. In the range p<n-2 its image and kernel are determined by the abutment filtration and incoming spectral-sequence differentials.

stages.title: Linear stability and finite quotients
stages.description:
Uniform degree bounds for Hurwitz homology: For every p,q>=0, deg H_q(K(M_p))<=A2+A0(3p+q), with constants chosen independently of k. For p>0 one has the stronger low-degree bounds deg H_0 K(M_p),deg H_1 K(M_p)<=A2+3A0 p.

Marked Hurwitz homological stability: For finite G and a nonsplitting class c, choose the actual central sum U_D and let a=Dd. There exist nonnegative integers A,B depending only on (G,c), independent of all fields k with |G| invertible, such that U_D:H_p(Hur_n;k)->H_p(Hur_(n+a);k) is an isomorphism whenever n>Ap+B, for every p,n>=0. For the fixed group the proof permits A=3A0 and B=A2+A0+2; these may subsequently be enlarged for the subgroup induction. U_D is the k-linear sum of power-block gluing maps.

Full-monodromy Hurwitz stability: Choose D simultaneously for all subgroups generated by their intersections with c. After enlarging A,B depending only on (G,c), the same U_D restricts to an isomorphism H_p(CHur_n;k)->H_p(CHur_(n+a);k) for n>Ap+B. The diagonal operator on the exact-H monodromy stratum is U_H=sum_(g∈c∩H) r_g^(Dd), viewed in the component ring for (H,c∩H). There is no factor |c|/|c∩H|.

Homology of the simultaneous-conjugation quotient: For X=Hur_n or CHur_n, with finite G and |G| invertible in k, the comparison X//G->X/G induces a homology isomorphism and H_p(X/G;k) ≅ H_p(X;k)_G. On an exact-H tuple stratum the point stabilizer is C_G(H). On CHur_n it is Z(G), so the G-action on CHur_n is free if G is center-free. There is no claim that the G-action on all Hur_n is free.

Unmarked Hurwitz homological stability: Assume G is center-free and c is nonsplitting. For every permitted coefficient field k, U_D induces isomorphisms H_p(Hur_n/G;k)->H_p(Hur_(n+a)/G;k) and H_p(CHur_n/G;k)->H_p(CHur_(n+a)/G;k) whenever n>Ap+B, with the common field-independent constants above.

stages.title: Finite-cell models and uniform etale Betti numbers
stages.description:
A finite-cell model for Hurwitz covers: For n>=2 construct the type-A Salvetti model Z_n of Conf_n using W=S_n with adjacent transpositions S={s_1,...,s_(n-1)}. Let P_n consist of (w,T), w∈W,T⊆S. Its strict order is (w,T)<(v,U) when T is a proper subset of U, w^-1 v belongs to the parabolic subgroup W_U, and length(t w^-1 v)>length(w^-1 v) for every t∈T. Define Z_n=|orderComplex(P_n)|/W for the free left W-action. Give it the coarser CW structure with one q-cell for each q-element T⊆S, using the corresponding parabolic permutohedra as characteristic cells. Establish Z_n≃Conf_n. Set Z_0 and Z_1 to a point. Lift this model along each parent finite covering Hur_n, CHur_n and their unmarked quotients of Conf_n; each lifted model has at most (2|G|)^n cells.

A uniform field Betti bound: Let A,B,a be the common nonnegative integer stability constants for the four spaces, and put K=2|G|, C=K^(A+B+a+1). For center-free finite G and nonsplitting c, every permitted coefficient field k and every i,n>=0 satisfy dim_k H_i(CHur_n/G;k)<=C^(i+1). The same argument bounds the other three variants with the appropriate marked or unmarked stability hypotheses. The constants depend only on (G,c).

Uniform etale Betti numbers: Assume G is finite and center-free, c is a rational nonidentity single generating nonsplitting conjugacy class, q is a prime power with characteristic coprime to |G|, and L is a prime with L>max(|G|,q,n). For the parent arithmetic Hurwitz scheme Hn_(G,n)^c of connected tame G-covers of the affine line, allowing ramification or no ramification at infinity as in IG.5, there is C=C(G,c) such that dim_(Q_L) H_et^i(Hn_(G,n)^c over algebraic_closure(F_q),Q_L)<=C^(i+1) for every i,n>=0. The same bound holds with F_L coefficients. This is a dimension theorem; its proof supplies no Frobenius-equivariant stabilization.
